english.title: Induce or procure person to vote in person at election when proxy already voted or entitled to vote by post
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you knowingly induced or procured a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to vote as elector in person at a

(A)_[parliamentary]_
(B)_[local government]_

election, namely **(..SPECIFY ELECTION..), knowing that a person appointed to vote as

(C)_[his]_
(D)_[her]_

proxy at the election, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),

(E)_[had already voted in person]_
(F)_[was entitled to vote by post]_

at that election
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 61(2)(c), (5) and (7) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowingly induced or procured a person to vote as elector in person at a parliamentary or local government election
knowing that a person appointed to vote as his/her proxy at the election
had already voted in person or was entitled to vote by post at that election

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
61(7) An offence under this section shall be an illegal practice but -
(a) the court before whom a person is convicted of any such offence may, if they think it just in the special circumstances of the case, mitigate or entirely remit any incapacity imposed by virtue of section 173; and (b) a candidate shall not be liable, nor shall his election be avoided, for an illegal practice under this section of any agent of his other than an offence under subsection (5) above.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 176

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
